Treatment summary
Patient presented following a rear impact sustained while the vehicle was turning
left, with subsequent complaints of neck pain, stiffness, and limited cervical range
of motion. The described mechanism is consistent with the reported neck strain. Over
the course of care the patient attended 29 visits, consisting of manual therapy,
therapeutic exercise, and home exercise instruction. The treatment pattern followed a
typical recovery trajectory, with visit frequency reduced as symptoms and mobility
improved. Examination findings include paraspinal muscle tenderness and reduced
rotation, which support the reported injury, while neurological screening and several
orthopedic provocation tests returned normal results. No prior injury to the cervical
region is known to this provider. Note that two similar service charges appearing on
the same date of service are under review for accuracy and are not yet resolved.
Discharge plan includes continued independent home exercise and return to usual
activities as tolerated.
</page>

Rate each feature below that THIS page gives evidence about. Leave out a feature the page
says nothing about. The ratings are listed from least to most suspicious.
- injury_crash_fit: Does the claimed injury fit the type and force of the crash? Allowed: Strong, Reasonable, Unclear, Inconsistent.
- treatment_growth: Did the treatment grow beyond what this injury needs? Allowed: Normal, Elevated, Disproportionate, Extreme.
- objective_support: Do objective tests (imaging, exam findings) support the complaints? Allowed: Strong, Partial, Predominantly subjective, Contradicted.
- pre_existing_condition: Did an earlier condition of the same body area add to the complaints? Allowed: None, Minor, Material, Predominant.
- duplicate_billing: Was the same service, visit or part billed twice? Allowed: None, Possible, Confirmed.
